data.one_liner: Extended network tools and scanning features for Flutter supporting iOS and Android.
data.what_it_does: Extends the network_tools package for Flutter to provide local network features such as pinging devices, scanning ports, ARP table lookup, and mDNS discovery. It runs host scans in a single isolate and handles background vendor table building.
use_when: You need to discover host devices and pingable addresses on a local subnet within a Flutter app.
You need to scan ports and query ARP tables on iOS, Android, Windows, macOS, or Linux.
avoid_when: You only need high-level REST, GraphQL, or WebSocket communication with remote servers.
You are building a sandboxed Mac App Store app where local network ARP access is restricted.
strengths: Supports multi-platform local network discovery including iOS, Android, Windows, macOS, and Linux.
Performs heavy host scans in isolated worker threads to prevent UI jank.
Provides mDNS search and service-type enumeration features.
weaknesses: Requires specific platform configurations and permissions (such as NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription and Bonjour services on iOS).
macOS sandboxing limitations can prevent MAC address lookup through the system ARP table.
data.setup_notes: Requires initializing the package with an application support directory path. Android and iOS require specific local network permissions and Bonjour service configuration in Info.plist / AndroidManifest.xml.
